mainTopic: When may we sell something that a buyer might misuse? This covers sales during שביעית, sales to someone suspected of reselling to gentiles, and sales of weapons.
overview: The גמרא brings a משנה in שביעית as proof that we may assume a buyer will use an animal in a permitted way. רבה rejects the proof by distinguishing cases where a person is commanded to let something rest. אביי (a field) and רב אשי (tools) knock down that distinction. רב אשי then gives a new rule: we assume a permitted use whenever one is realistic, and only then. Next comes a story: רבה sold a donkey to a Jew suspected of selling animals to gentiles. אביי proves from two ברייתות about כותים that one may not sell to someone likely to pass the item on to a gentile. A ruling of רב נחמן settles it, and רבה runs after the buyer to undo the sale, without success. The amud ends with רב דימי בר אבא's ban on selling weapons to a Jewish robber and a ברייתא about selling shields, where רב's explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Proof that we assume the buyer will use the animal in a permitted way
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for a source for the idea that we assume a buyer will use an animal for a permitted purpose. It cites בית הלל, who permit selling a plowing cow in שביעית because the buyer might slaughter it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And where do you see that we reason this way? From the משנה: בית שמאי say a person may not sell a plowing cow during שביעית, and בית הלל permit it, because the buyer can slaughter it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wants a source for the earlier idea that we may assume an animal is bought for slaughter. It brings one from a משנה about שביעית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Plowing is forbidden in שביעית, so a plowing cow looks like it is being bought for a forbidden job. Still, בית הלל allow the sale, because the buyer might simply slaughter the cow. The proof is that we give the buyer the benefit of the doubt and assume a permitted use.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do you say this? (asking for a source)
The seventh year, when working the land is forbidden

steps.whyThisMatters: Since the הלכה follows בית הלל, this would show that we may assume a buyer intends a permitted use.

phrases.english: And from where do you say
that we say this in a case like this?
phrases.notes: He means the earlier idea that we assume the animal was bought to be slaughtered.

phrases.english: As we learned in a משנה: בית שמאי say:
A person may not sell a plowing cow
during the seventh year,
and בית הלל permit it,
because he can slaughter it.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמְנָא תֵּימְרָא דְּאָמְרִינַן כִּי הַאי גַוְונָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the earlier claim that an animal may be assumed to be bought for slaughter.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that we assume a buyer will use an animal for a permitted purpose.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in שביעית where בית הלל permit selling a plowing cow because the buyer can slaughter it.

steps.title: רבה: the two cases are not comparable
steps.stepSummary: רבה rejects the proof. In שביעית there is no command to let one's animal rest, but on שבת there is.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said: Are these cases the same? There, in שביעית, a person is not commanded to let his animal rest. Here, a person is commanded to let his animal rest on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה pushes back on the proof from step 1. He says the שביעית case is different from selling an animal to a non-Jew.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In שביעית the Torah does not command a person about his animal resting, so the only worry is the buyer's own sin, and we assume he will slaughter the cow. On שבת a person is commanded about שביתת בהמה, so selling an animal to a non-Jew carries an extra worry of its own. Because of that worry, it stays forbidden even if the buyer might slaughter it.

phrases.english: רבה said: Are these comparable?
There, a person is not commanded
about letting his animal rest in the seventh year,
here, a person is commanded
about letting his animal rest on שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 1.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The comparison between the שביעית cow and selling an animal to a non-Jew.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: On שבת there is a personal command to let one's animal rest, but in שביעית there is not.

steps.title: אביי: a field must rest, yet selling it is allowed
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רבה with the case of a field. A person is commanded to let his field rest in שביעית, yet בית הלל permit selling a plowed field because the buyer may leave it unplanted.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Is it true that wherever a person is commanded, the sale is forbidden? There is a field: a person is commanded to let his field rest in שביעית. Yet we learned that בית שמאי say a person may not sell a plowed field in שביעית, and בית הלל permit it, because the buyer can leave it unplanted.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רבה's rule that "commanded means forbidden." He brings a case where there is a command, yet the sale is still allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה implied that once a person is commanded about something's resting, he may not sell it to someone who might work it. But a person is commanded to let his own field rest in שביעית, and בית הלל still permit selling a plowed field, assuming the buyer will leave it alone. So being commanded does not automatically make the sale forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: But look at this case (introducing a counterexample)
A plowed field ready for planting

phrases.english: אביי said to him:
And wherever a person is commanded, it is forbidden?
But there is a field,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָדָם מְצוֶּּוה עַל שְׁבִיתַת שָׂדֵהוּ בַּשְּׁבִיעִית,
phrases.english: where a person is commanded to let his field rest in the seventh year,
and we learned: בית שמאי say:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא יִמְכּוֹר אָדָם שְׂדֵה נִיר בַּשְּׁבִיעִית,
phrases.english: A person may not sell a plowed field in the seventh year,
and בית הלל permit it,
because he can leave it unplanted!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: וְכֹל הֵיכָא דְּאָדָם מְצוֶּּוה אָסוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's distinction from step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's rule that where a person is commanded about resting, the sale is forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A field must rest in שביעית, yet בית הלל permit selling it, so a command does not automatically forbid the sale.

steps.title: רב אשי: tools need not rest, yet selling them is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי challenges רבה from the other direction. There is no command to let tools rest in שביעית, yet a משנה forbids selling plowing tools.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי objects: Is it true that wherever a person is not commanded, the sale is allowed? There are tools: a person is not commanded to let his tools rest in שביעית. Yet we learned: these are the tools a person may not sell in שביעית: the plow and all its parts, the yoke, the winnowing fork, and the digging stake.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי attacks the other half of רבה's rule, that "not commanded means allowed." He brings a case where there is no command, yet the sale is forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבה's logic, anything a person is not commanded to rest should be fine to sell, just like the cow. But tools have no command of rest, and the משנה still forbids selling them in שביעית. So the presence or absence of a command does not decide the matter.
steps.whatToRemember: רבה tried to split the cases by whether a person is commanded to let the item rest. אביי (field) and רב אשי (tools) show that this split does not fit the sources in either direction.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two challenges. אביי shows a command where the sale is still allowed. רב אשי shows no command where the sale is still forbidden.

phrases.english: רב אשי challenges it:

phrases.aramaic: וְכֹל הֵיכָא דְּאֵין אָדָם מְצוֶּּוה — שְׁרֵי?
phrases.english: And wherever a person is not commanded, it is permitted?
But there are tools,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאֵין אָדָם מְצוֶּּוה עַל שְׁבִיתַת כֵּלִים בִּשְׁבִיעִית,
phrases.english: where a person is not commanded to let tools rest in the seventh year,
and we learned:

phrases.aramaic: אֵלּוּ הֵן כֵּלִים שֶׁאֵין אָדָם רַשַּׁאי
phrases.english: These are the tools that a person is not allowed
to sell in the seventh year:
the plow and all its parts,
the yoke, the winnowing fork, and the digging stake!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב אָשֵׁי: וְכֹל הֵיכָא דְּאֵין אָדָם מְצוֶּּוה שְׁרֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge to רבה, from the opposite direction of אביי's.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's implication that where there is no command to rest, the sale is permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Tools have no command of rest in שביעית, yet the משנה forbids selling plowing tools, so the lack of a command does not make the sale allowed.

steps.title: רב אשי's rule: assume a permitted use only when one is realistic
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי drops רבה's distinction about a command to let things rest. The only question is whether a permitted use is realistic.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב אשי said: wherever there is a realistic permitted use to assume, we assume it, even if there is a command to let the item rest. Wherever there is no such use, we do not assume one, even if there is no command to let the item rest.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי replaces רבה's rejected distinction with a new, simpler rule that fits all the cases from the earlier steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה said the difference depends on whether there is a command to let the item rest. But the field (Step 3) and the tools (Step 4) showed that this does not work. רב אשי says the only question is whether the buyer has a realistic permitted use: a cow can be slaughtered and a field can be left fallow, but plowing tools have no other use.

keyTerms.meaning: to attribute or assume (a permitted reason or use)
commanded (here: commanded to let the item rest)

steps.whatToRemember: The rule is not about whether there is a command to let the item rest. It is about whether a realistic permitted use exists. If one exists, we assume it. If not, we do not.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule explains the cow, the field and the tools together, and it replaces רבה's rejected distinction.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Ashi said:
Anywhere that there is room to assume a permitted use, we assume it,
even though one is commanded to let it rest,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֹל הֵיכָא דְּלֵיכָּא לְמִיתְלֵי — לָא תָּלֵינַן,
phrases.english: and anywhere that there is no room to assume one, we do not assume it,
even though one is not commanded to let it rest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רב אשי himself challenged רבה (Step 4), he offers a replacement rule.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Whether we assume a permitted use depends only on whether one is realistic, not on whether there is a command to let the item rest.

steps.title: רבה sells a donkey and אביי asks why
steps.stepSummary: רבה sold a donkey to a Jew suspected of selling large animals to gentiles, and אביי asks him why.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה sold a certain donkey to a Jew who was suspected of selling large animals to gentiles. אביי said to him: Why did the Master do this?
steps.whatsHappening: A new story begins. אביי questions רבה about a sale that looks problematic, and this sets up the back-and-forth that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Selling a large animal directly to a gentile is not allowed. The buyer here is a Jew, but he has a reputation for passing such animals on to gentiles. So אביי wants to know how רבה could sell to him.

phrases.english: Rabba sold a certain donkey
to a Jew who was suspected of selling to a gentile.
Abaye said to him:
What is the reason the Master acted this way?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new story related to the same theme of what we suspect a buyer will do.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבה allowed himself to sell a large animal to someone suspected of selling to gentiles.

steps.title: רבה: I sold it to a Jew
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that his sale was to a Jew, not to a gentile.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה said to him: I sold it to a Jew.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה defends himself. He did nothing wrong, because the person he sold to is Jewish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה looks only at the sale itself. The prohibition is selling to a gentile, and he sold to a Jew.

phrases.english: He said to him:
I sold it to a Jew.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The sale was to a Jew, so the ban on selling to gentiles does not apply.

steps.title: אביי: but he will sell it to a gentile
steps.stepSummary: אביי pushes back: this buyer will just go and sell the donkey to a gentile.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: But he will go and sell it to a gentile!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רבה's answer by pointing to what the buyer is likely to do next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי argues that selling to a Jew is not enough if that Jew is known to pass animals on to gentiles. In his view, the buyer's reputation should count against the sale.

phrases.english: He said to him:
But he will go and sell it to a gentile!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבה's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's claim that selling to a Jew is fine.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The buyer is known to sell to gentiles, so the animal will likely end up with a gentile anyway.

steps.title: רבה: he could just as well sell it to a Jew
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers that there is no reason to assume the buyer will sell to a gentile and not to a Jew.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה answered: Does he only sell to gentiles? Doesn't he also sell to Jews?
steps.whatsHappening: רבה defends his sale. The suspected buyer also sells to Jews, so we do not have to assume the worst.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבה reasons that where a permitted outcome is realistic, we assume it. Since the buyer could just as easily sell the donkey to another Jew, רבה holds the sale is permitted. The גמרא goes on to reject this in Step 17, and in Step 18 רבה himself runs after the buyer to undo the sale.

phrases.english: Does he sell only to a gentile,
and not sell to a Jew?

steps.triggerLanguage: לְגוֹי קָא מְזַבֵּין, לְיִשְׂרָאֵל לָא קָא מְזַבֵּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the assumption behind the challenge
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A suspected seller will surely pass the animal to a gentile.
steps.terutzMaskana: He could equally sell it to a Jew, so we do not assume the forbidden outcome.

steps.title: אביי cites the law of selling small animals to כותים
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes a ברייתא: selling small animals to כותים depends on local custom. The גמרא asks for the reason and suggests it may be that they are suspected of רביעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי raised an objection: In a place where people sell small animals to כותים, one may sell. Where they do not, one may not sell. What is the reason? If you say it is because they are suspected of רביעה...
steps.whatsHappening: אביי starts a challenge to רבה from a ברייתא. Before the challenge can land, the גמרא needs the reason for the ban, so it begins testing a possible reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In some places the ברייתא forbids selling small animals to כותים, even though selling them is not forbidden in itself. That suggests we do suspect a buyer of misuse, which would go against רבה. The first reason suggested is that כותים are suspected of רביעה.

phrases.english: He raised an objection to him:
In a place where people were accustomed to sell
small livestock to Samaritans, one may sell;
where they were accustomed not to sell, one may not sell.
What is the reason?
If you say it is because they are suspected of bestiality,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: אביי challenges רבה's lenient answer from a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבה's assumption that we do not suspect the buyer.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא forbids a sale in some places out of suspicion about the buyer. The גמרא first needs to identify which suspicion that is.

steps.title: Are כותים really suspected? A ברייתא on gentiles
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions whether כותים are suspected of רביעה and quotes a ברייתא. Its first half lists restrictions with gentiles.
steps.simpleTranslation: But are they suspected? Isn't it taught: One may not keep an animal in gentiles' inns, male animals near men or female animals near women, and certainly not female near men or male near women. One may not hand an animal to their shepherd, may not be alone with them, and may not give them a child to teach him reading or a craft.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the suggested reason from Step 10 by quoting a ברייתא. This first part sets up the contrast between gentiles and כותים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists strict rules about gentiles: animals may not be left in their inns, and certain contact with them is forbidden. These rules about gentiles are the background for the contrast with כותים that comes next.

phrases.english: But are they suspected?
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
One may not keep an animal
in the inns of gentiles:
male animals with men,
phrases.notes: Literally 'males with males.' The first word means the animals, and the second means the people at the inn.

phrases.english: and female animals with women,
and needless to say,

phrases.aramaic: נְקֵבוֹת אֵצֶל זְכָרִים וּזְכָרִים אֵצֶל נְקֵבוֹת.
phrases.english: female animals with men and male animals with women.
And one may not hand an animal over to their shepherd,
and one may not be alone with them,
and one may not hand a child over to them
to teach him reading or to teach him a craft,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the reason suggested in Step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that כותים are suspected of רביעה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא treats gentiles strictly but, as its next line shows, treats כותים leniently.

steps.title: The ברייתא permits keeping animals in the inns of כותים
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: animals may be kept in the inns of כותים, even male animals near women and female animals near men. This shows כותים are not suspected of רביעה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But one may keep an animal in the inns of כותים, male animals near women and female animals near men, and certainly male near men and female near women.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the key line of the ברייתא. It proves that כותים are not suspected of רביעה, so the reason suggested in Step 10 cannot be right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For gentiles the ברייתא forbids even the less worrying arrangements. For כותים it permits even the more worrying ones. So suspicion of רביעה cannot explain the ban on selling small animals to כותים, and the גמרא will need another reason.

phrases.english: but one may keep an animal
in the inns of Samaritans:
male animals with women
and female animals with men,
and needless to say,

phrases.aramaic: זְכָרִים אֵצֶל זְכָרִים וּנְקֵבוֹת אֵצֶל נְקֵבוֹת.
phrases.english: male animals with men and female animals with women.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל מַעֲמִידִין בְּהֵמָה בְּפוּנְדְּקָאוֹת שֶׁל כּוּתִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in Step 11 and gives the decisive contrast.
steps.raayaObject: That כותים are not suspected of רביעה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא permitting animals to be kept in the inns of כותים, even male animals with women and female animals with men.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two lists. Gentiles are treated strictly, and even the 'safer' arrangements are forbidden. כותים are treated leniently, and even the 'riskier' arrangements are allowed.

steps.title: The ברייתא ends: כותים are trusted, so they are not suspected
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא adds that one may give an animal to a כותי shepherd, be alone with כותים, and send a child to them to learn. The גמרא concludes that כותים are not suspected.
steps.simpleTranslation: We may hand an animal to their shepherd, be alone with them, and give them a child to teach him reading and a trade. So clearly they are not suspected.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the ברייתא from the last step and draws its conclusion: כותים are not suspected of רביעה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Trusting a כותי shepherd with an animal shows they are not suspected of רביעה. So if there is a custom against selling them small animals, the reason must be something else: they might resell the animal to a גוי. That backs up אביי's challenge to רבה.

keyTerms.meaning: One may be alone with them in private

phrases.english: And one may hand over an animal to their shepherd,
and one may be alone with them,
and one may hand over a child to them
to teach him reading and to teach him a trade;
evidently, they are not suspected.
phrases.notes: He means not suspected of רביעה, so the worry must be that they will resell to a גוי.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא begun in steps 11-12 and states what it proves.
steps.raayaObject: That כותים are not suspected of רביעה, so the ban on selling them animals is about reselling to a גוי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ending of the ברייתא allowing one to trust כותים with animals, to be alone with them, and to send children to them.

steps.title: A second ברייתא: no selling weapons to a גוי or a כותי
steps.stepSummary: Another ברייתא forbids selling weapons, weapon equipment, and chains to both a גוי and a כותי.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught: we do not sell them weapons or weapon equipment, we do not sharpen weapons for them, and we do not sell them stocks, neck chains, foot chains, or iron chains. This applies to both a גוי and a כותי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא to support אביי. It sets up the next question: why does this ban include a כותי?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on weapons and chains makes sense for a גוי. The surprise is that it includes a כותי too. The next steps will figure out why.

keyTerms.meaning: Stocks, a wooden frame used to lock a prisoner's feet

phrases.english: And furthermore, it was taught:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין מוֹכְרִין לָהֶם לֹא זַיִין וְלֹא כְּלֵי זַיִין,
phrases.english: one may not sell them weapons or weapon equipment,
and one may not sharpen weapons for them,
and one may not sell them stocks
nor neck chains nor foot chains
nor iron chains,
both a gentile and a Samaritan.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second source after the first ברייתא was finished.
steps.raayaObject: That a seller must worry a buyer will pass items on to a גוי.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא forbidding the sale of weapons and chains to both a גוי and a כותי.

steps.title: Is the reason that כותים are suspected of murder? No
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why weapons may not be sold to a כותי. It suggests they are suspected of murder, then rejects this because the earlier ברייתא allows being alone with them.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? If you say they are suspected of murder, are they really? You said one may be alone with them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the weapons ban for a כותי and knocks down the first suggestion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If כותים were suspected of שפיכות דמים, one could not be alone with them. But the earlier ברייתא allowed exactly that. So murder cannot be the reason.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
If we say that they are suspected of bloodshed,
but are they suspected?
Didn't you say: and one may be alone with them!
phrases.notes: This points back to the line in step 13 of the earlier ברייתא.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא? אִי נֵימָא דַּחֲשִׁידִי אַשְּׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks at the weapons ברייתא and tests a possible reason against the first ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that weapons are banned for כותים because they are suspected of murder.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first ברייתא lets one be alone with כותים, which would not be allowed if they were suspected of murder.

steps.title: The real reason: the כותי will resell to a גוי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes the ban exists because the כותי might sell the weapon to a גוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it is because he will come to sell it to a גוי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the true reason for the weapons ban: worry about reselling to a גוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This proves the principle אביי needs: a seller must worry about a buyer who might pass the item on to a גוי. That applies directly to רבה, who sold his donkey to a Jew suspected of selling to גוים.

phrases.english: Rather, it is because he will come to sell it to a gentile.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15 after its first suggestion failed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why weapons may not be sold to a כותי.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Because the כותי might resell them to a גוי.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets up the rule that one may not sell to someone likely to pass the item to a forbidden buyer.

steps.title: No split between a כותי and a Jew
steps.stepSummary: Someone might say a כותי will not repent but a Jew will, so a Jew can be trusted. The גמרא rejects this using רב נחמן's statement in the name of רבה בר אבוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say a כותי won't repent but a Jew will, didn't רב נחמן say in the name of רבה בר אבוה: just as it is forbidden to sell to a גוי, so it is forbidden to sell to a Jew suspected of selling to a גוי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shuts down a possible defense of רבה: that a Jewish buyer is different from a כותי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggested split was that a Jew might do תשובה and stop selling to גוים. But רב נחמן says outright that selling to a suspected Jew is forbidden, just like selling to a גוי. So רבה's sale cannot be defended.
steps.confusionAlert: רבה בר אבוה, quoted here by רב נחמן, is a different person from רבה, who sold the donkey.

phrases.english: And if you would say:
a Samaritan does not repent,
a Jew does repent,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: but didn't Rav Nachman say that Rabba bar Avuh said:
just as they said it is forbidden to sell to a gentile,
so too it is forbidden to sell to a Jew
who is suspected of selling to a gentile!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: כּוּתִי לָא עָבֵיד תְּשׁוּבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Blocks a possible way to keep the proof from step 16 from applying to a Jewish buyer.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proposed difference between a כותי buyer and a Jewish buyer.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב נחמן rules directly that a Jew suspected of selling to a גוי is treated like a גוי.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical rule: one may not sell to a Jew who is suspected of passing the item on to a גוי.

steps.title: רבה runs after the buyer of his donkey
steps.stepSummary: רבה accepts the challenge and runs a long way after the buyer to cancel the sale, but cannot catch him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He ran after him three parasangs; some say one parasang through sand. And he did not catch him.
steps.whatsHappening: The story ends: רבה accepts אביי's argument and tries to undo his donkey sale.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By running after the buyer, רבה shows he now agrees the sale was forbidden. Whether he ran three parasangs or one parasang through sand, which is slow going, he made a great effort. Still, he could not reach the buyer.

keyTerms.meaning: A parasang, a measure of distance of several kilometers

steps.whatToRemember: One may not sell to a Jew suspected of selling to a גוי, just as one may not sell to the גוי directly. רבה himself accepted this and ran after his buyer.

phrases.english: He ran after him three parasangs,
phrases.notes: רבה is running after the man who bought his donkey, hoping to cancel the sale.

phrases.english: and some say: one parasang through sand,
and he did not catch up to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows רבה accepting the argument completed in step 17.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבה agrees it was forbidden to sell his donkey to a Jew suspected of selling to גוים, and tries to undo the sale.

steps.title: Weapons may not be sold to a Jewish bandit either
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי בר אבא rules that the ban on selling weapons to a גוי also applies to a Jewish bandit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב דימי בר אבא said: Just as it is forbidden to sell weapons to a גוי, it is forbidden to sell them to a Jewish bandit.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teacher, רב דימי בר אבא, adds to the weapons ban. He says the same ban also covers a Jewish bandit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the ban was about a גוי and a כותי. רב דימי בר אבא widens it to a Jew who lives as a bandit. The next step will ask which kind of bandit he means.

keyTerms.meaning: Just as, in the same way that

phrases.english: Rav Dimi bar Abba said:
Just as it is forbidden to sell to a gentile,
phrases.notes: He means selling weapons, like in the ברייתא from step 14.

phrases.english: it is forbidden to sell to a Jewish bandit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a related ruling to the weapons ban discussed in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Weapons may not be sold to a Jewish bandit, just as they may not be sold to a גוי.

steps.title: Which kind of bandit is meant?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא sets up a two-sided problem. If the bandit kills, the ruling is obvious. If he does not kill, why is it forbidden?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If he is suspected of killing, it is obvious, because he is just like a גוי. And if he does not kill, why should it be forbidden?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what kind of bandit רב דימי בר אבא is talking about. Both possible answers seem to cause a problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the bandit is a killer, he is no different from a גוי, so there was no need to say this at all. If he never kills, there seems to be no reason to stop selling to him. So the ruling looks either unnecessary or unjustified.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What situation are we talking about?
It is obvious, so why say it?

phrases.english: What is the case?
If he is suspected of killing,
it is obvious; he is just like a gentile.
And if he does not kill,
why not sell to him?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב דימי בר אבא's ruling by questioning what case it could be about.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב דימי בר אבא's ruling about a Jewish bandit
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two-sided problem: a killer makes the ruling obvious, and a non-killer makes the ruling seem baseless.

steps.title: A robber who might kill to save himself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the bandit does not normally kill, but he is a robber who might use the weapon to save himself if caught.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, he is a bandit who does not kill. Here we are dealing with a robber, because sometimes he uses the weapon to save himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the problem. The bandit is not a killer, but he is a robber who might kill if someone catches him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This picks the second side, a bandit who does not kill, and explains why the ruling still makes sense. A robber does not plan to kill, but when he is caught he may use the weapon to save his own life. So the ruling is neither obvious nor baseless.

keyTerms.meaning: Really, actually, it is still the case that
What case are we dealing with here?
A robber who grabs and steals

phrases.english: Really, it is one who does not kill,
and what are we dealing with here?
With a robber,
for sometimes he uses it to save himself.
phrases.notes: He means he might kill with the weapon when he gets caught.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם דְּלָא קָטֵיל, וְהָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the two-sided problem by choosing the non-killer case and giving it a reason.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A bandit who does not kill poses no danger, so there is no reason to ban selling to him.
steps.terutzMaskana: A robber may kill in self-defense when caught, so weapons may not be sold to him.
steps.whatToRemember: רב דימי בר אבא's ban covers a Jewish robber who does not plan to kill, because he might kill to save himself if caught.

steps.title: A disagreement about selling shields
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings two opinions: one forbids selling shields to גוים, and the יש אומרים allow it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: One may not sell shields to them. And some say: One may sell shields to them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about shields. It records a disagreement over whether shields count as forbidden weapons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A shield protects. It does not attack. The first opinion still forbids selling shields to גוים, and the יש אומרים permit it. The next step asks for the reason behind the first opinion.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One may not sell shields to them,
and some say:
One may sell shields to them.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֵין מוֹכְרִין לָהֶן תְּרִיסִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new ברייתא about a related item, shields, within the weapons-selling topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: There is a disagreement: one opinion forbids selling shields to גוים, and another permits it.

steps.title: Why forbid shields? Then food should be forbidden too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason shields are forbidden. If it is because they protect the גוים, then wheat and barley should also be forbidden. רב's answer is introduced.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? If you say it is because shields protect them, then even wheat and barley should not be sold to them! רב said:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the first opinion forbids shields, and it attacks the obvious reason. The last words, "רב said," set up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A shield only helps the גוים survive. If that alone were a problem, then food, which also helps them survive, would be forbidden too, and it is not. So there must be some other reason, and רב is about to give it.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying food is forbidden. It is pointing out that food is clearly allowed, so "it protects them" cannot be the real reason for the shield ban.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
If you say it is because they protect them,
if so,
even wheat and barley should also not be sold!
Rav said:

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא? אִילֵּימָא מִשּׁוּם דְּמַגְּנוּ עֲלַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the first opinion in the shields ברייתא and rejects the simple explanation. It then sets up רב's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The first opinion in the ברייתא, which forbids selling shields
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If protecting the גוים were the reason, then food, which also helps them survive, would be forbidden too. That cannot be right.
